% Fixture for #138, extended by #147 — a control sheet shaped like a real one.
%
% This is what the generator will emit from the question bank: a pool of twelve
% questions for a section range, of which each copy draws four at random, with
% the alternatives shuffled too (docs/design/2026-08-controles.md §C6).
%
% The pool carries one question of EACH kind the bank can hold — ten with a
% single correct answer, one with several (`comparar-cadenas`), and one whose
% statement includes code read from its own file (`suma-arreglo`). That is not
% decoration: every one of those shapes broke something the first time it was
% compiled or read, and a shape absent from this file is a shape nothing in
% the suite exercises.
%
% Content is Spanish because a control sheet is course material and a student
% reads it (apps/amc-worker/CLAUDE.md §Language). Macro names are AMC's English
% aliases — the .sty provides both those and the original French ones.
%
% The RUT grid is eight digits and carries no verifier digit: `\AMCcode` is
% digits-only and a DV can be K, and with an enrolled-student list the body
% alone identifies the student (§C5).

\documentclass[letterpaper,11pt]{article}

\usepackage[utf8]{inputenc}
\usepackage[T1]{fontenc}
\usepackage[spanish]{babel}
\usepackage{multicol}
\usepackage{listings}
% lang=ES is not cosmetic: without it AMC labels every question "Question 1" in
% English, on a sheet a Spanish-speaking student reads. Measured in #138 S2 —
% the first compile shipped English labels past a green run, because nothing
% about a wrong-language label makes LaTeX fail.
%
% `completemulti` is deliberately ABSENT (#147). It made AMC append its own
% "none of these" box to every multiple-answer question: all-or-nothing, in
% Spanish it got wrong ("Ninguna de estas preguntas son correctas"), and it
% gave that appended box the index 0, so a multiple's boxes ran 0..N while a
% simple question's ran 1..N — measured, the authored alternatives keep 1..N
% either way, so a 1-based reader dropped the box rather than shifting anything.
% A question that wants that alternative writes
% it by hand, in our Spanish, as one more choice — see `comparar-cadenas`.
\usepackage[box,lang=ES]{automultiplechoice}

% What each question says about itself, and the asymmetry behind it. A student
% has five minutes and cannot scroll back to learn a convention, so the type is
% stated per question, in words, for BOTH kinds — a symbol needs a legend, and
% a legend is read once at the top and forgotten by question three.
%
% It takes two different levers, which looks like a bug the first time it is
% met. A simple question takes the label as its optional argument. A
% `questionmult` CANNOT: measured, and the .sty says why — its definition
% already passes `\multiSymbole` into that same slot (automultiplechoice.sty
% line 1232), so a second one mangles the text. Redefining `\multiSymbole` is
% the supported way in, and it replaces AMC's default club suit.
\def\unaSymbole{\textsf{\small(una respuesta)}}
\def\multiSymbole{\textsf{\small(varias respuestas)}}

% Code inside an AMC question must arrive from a FILE. `verbatim` does not
% compile inside a question environment, and the way it fails is the trap: the
% first attempt compiled only because the random draw did not pick that
% question, so a real control would have broken on the day it drew it (#147).
% `\lstinputlisting` is also the shape the question bank is built for — code as
% its own field, so nothing has to be escaped.
\lstset{
  basicstyle=\ttfamily\small,
  columns=fullflexible,
  keepspaces=true,
  xleftmargin=1em,
}

% Fixed seed so a test run is reproducible: the same seed must produce the same
% four questions in the same order for copy N, every time. Without this, a
% failure could never be told apart from a different draw.
\AMCrandomseed{1242}

\begin{document}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
% The pool. In production these come from the published questions.json for the
% selected section range; here they stand in for it.
% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

\element{clase}{
  \begin{question}[\unaSymbole]{iteraciones}
    ¿Cuántas iteraciones hace, a lo más, la búsqueda binaria sobre un arreglo
    ordenado de $n$ elementos?
    \begin{choices}
      \correctchoice{Alrededor de $\log_2 n$}
      \wrongchoice{Alrededor de $n$}
      \wrongchoice{Alrededor de $n^2$}
      \wrongchoice{Siempre 2}
    \end{choices}
  \end{question}
}

\element{clase}{
  \begin{question}[\unaSymbole]{requisito}
    ¿Qué condición debe cumplir el arreglo para poder aplicar búsqueda binaria?
    \begin{choices}
      \correctchoice{Estar ordenado}
      \wrongchoice{No tener elementos repetidos}
      \wrongchoice{Tener un número par de elementos}
      \wrongchoice{Estar lleno}
    \end{choices}
  \end{question}
}

\element{clase}{
  \begin{question}[\unaSymbole]{lineal}
    En el peor caso, ¿cuántas comparaciones hace la búsqueda lineal sobre
    $n$ elementos?
    \begin{choices}
      \correctchoice{$n$}
      \wrongchoice{$\log_2 n$}
      \wrongchoice{$n/2$}
      \wrongchoice{1}
    \end{choices}
  \end{question}
}

\element{clase}{
  \begin{question}[\unaSymbole]{tipo-primitivo}
    En Java, ¿cuál de estos es un tipo primitivo?
    \begin{choices}
      \correctchoice{\texttt{int}}
      \wrongchoice{\texttt{String}}
      \wrongchoice{\texttt{Integer}}
      \wrongchoice{\texttt{Object}}
    \end{choices}
  \end{question}
}

\element{clase}{
  \begin{question}[\unaSymbole]{igualdad}
    En Java, ¿qué compara el operador \texttt{==} aplicado a dos objetos?
    \begin{choices}
      \correctchoice{Si son el mismo objeto}
      \wrongchoice{Si tienen el mismo contenido}
      \wrongchoice{Si son de la misma clase}
      \wrongchoice{Si ambos son distintos de \texttt{null}}
    \end{choices}
  \end{question}
}

\element{clase}{
  \begin{question}[\unaSymbole]{arreglo-largo}
    En Java, ¿cómo se obtiene la cantidad de elementos de un arreglo
    \texttt{a}?
    \begin{choices}
      \correctchoice{\texttt{a.length}}
      \wrongchoice{\texttt{a.length()}}
      \wrongchoice{\texttt{a.size()}}
      \wrongchoice{\texttt{len(a)}}
    \end{choices}
  \end{question}
}

\element{clase}{
  \begin{question}[\unaSymbole]{indice}
    ¿Cuál es el índice del primer elemento de un arreglo en Java?
    \begin{choices}
      \correctchoice{0}
      \wrongchoice{1}
      \wrongchoice{-1}
      \wrongchoice{Depende del tipo}
    \end{choices}
  \end{question}
}

\element{clase}{
  \begin{question}[\unaSymbole]{referencia}
    Si \texttt{b = a} y ambos son referencias al mismo objeto, ¿qué ocurre al
    modificar un campo a través de \texttt{b}?
    \begin{choices}
      \correctchoice{El cambio se ve también a través de \texttt{a}}
      \wrongchoice{\texttt{a} conserva el valor anterior}
      \wrongchoice{Se lanza una excepción}
      \wrongchoice{Se crea una copia del objeto}
    \end{choices}
  \end{question}
}

\element{clase}{
  \begin{question}[\unaSymbole]{descarte}
    En cada paso, la búsqueda binaria descarta:
    \begin{choices}
      \correctchoice{La mitad de los elementos que quedaban}
      \wrongchoice{Un elemento}
      \wrongchoice{Todos los mayores al buscado}
      \wrongchoice{Nada, solo avanza}
    \end{choices}
  \end{question}
}

\element{clase}{
  \begin{question}[\unaSymbole]{peor-caso}
    Sobre 1000 elementos ordenados, ¿cuántas iteraciones hace la búsqueda
    binaria en el peor caso?
    \begin{choices}
      \correctchoice{Alrededor de 10}
      \wrongchoice{Alrededor de 100}
      \wrongchoice{Alrededor de 500}
      \wrongchoice{Alrededor de 1000}
    \end{choices}
  \end{question}
}

% A question with SEVERAL correct alternatives. Its last choice is the
% "ninguna de las anteriores" AMC used to append on its own: written by hand
% here, in our own Spanish, and numbered like any other alternative.
\element{clase}{
  \begin{questionmult}{comparar-cadenas}
    En Java, ¿cuáles de estas expresiones comparan el \emph{contenido} de dos
    \texttt{String} \texttt{a} y \texttt{b}?
    \begin{choices}
      \correctchoice{\texttt{a.equals(b)}}
      \correctchoice{\texttt{a.compareTo(b) == 0}}
      \wrongchoice{\texttt{a == b}}
      % `\lastchoices` pins what follows at the end while the rest shuffle, and
      % it is not decoration: without it this alternative came out SECOND on
      % copy 1 — a "ninguna de las anteriores" printed above two of them, which
      % says something false to the student reading it. Found by rendering the
      % sheet and looking at it, not by any assertion. It is also the mechanism
      % AMC uses for the box `completemulti` appends (automultiplechoice.sty
      % line 867), so an alternative of this kind is pinned the same way whether
      % AMC writes it or we do.
      \lastchoices
      \wrongchoice{Ninguna de las anteriores}
    \end{choices}
  \end{questionmult}
}

% A question carrying code, read from its own file.
\element{clase}{
  \begin{question}[\unaSymbole]{suma-arreglo}
    ¿Qué imprime este programa?

    % ABSOLUTE, and measured: a path relative to this file does not resolve.
    % AMC compiles from its own working directory, so `src/code/…` fails with
    % "File `src/code/suma-arreglo(.java)' not found" and no PDF is produced.
    % Everything this worker is handed lives under /work by contract (README
    % §How it is driven), so that is the path a generated control will use too.
    \lstinputlisting{/work/src/code/suma-arreglo.java}
    \begin{choices}
      \correctchoice{20}
      \wrongchoice{8}
      \wrongchoice{4}
      \wrongchoice{0}
    \end{choices}
  \end{question}
}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
% The sheet. One per student, each drawing its own four questions.
% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

\onecopy{5}{

  \noindent{\large\bf Control de entrada}\hfill
  \namefield{\fbox{\begin{minipage}{.45\linewidth}
        Nombre:\dotfill
        \vspace*{2mm}
      \end{minipage}}}

  \begin{center}
    \emph{Marca tu RUT sin el dígito verificador (8 dígitos).}

    \AMCcode{rut}{8}
  \end{center}

  % This used to read "Marca una sola alternativa por pregunta", which stopped
  % being true the moment the pool held a multiple-answer question. What
  % replaces it is the instructions plus the total and how the total is
  % reached, with THIS sheet's numbers — nobody should have to do a rule of
  % three under a clock. WP-E computes them per generated control; the fixture
  % only has to stop saying something false.
  \vspace{3mm}
  \noindent\fbox{\begin{minipage}{0.98\linewidth}
      \textbf{4 preguntas} · \textbf{4 puntos} · el 4,0 son 2 puntos

      \smallskip
      Cada pregunta dice cuántas respuestas admite.
      \textbf{Respóndelas todas: equivocarse no descuenta.}
      \textbf{Rellena por completo el cuadrado de tu respuesta.}
      No marques con X ni con tilde.
    \end{minipage}}
  \vspace{2mm}

  \shufflegroup{clase}
  \insertgroup[4]{clase}

  \AMCcleardoublepage
}

\end{document}
